prose: The Verge's Decoder interviews Atlassian cofounder and CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes on the 'SaaSpocalypse' thesis and why he thinks chatbots are not the future of work. The bear case put to him: AI agents could read across all a company's tools directly, making migration to Atlassian's platform less enticing, or AI could simply build Jira/Trello-style tools on demand and destroy the category. Cannon-Brookes pushes back at length, arguing for the value of design and human users and claiming AI is increasing usage of Atlassian's tools. The conversation also covers Atlassian's new org chart - all products as expressions of a single core platform - and this year's layoffs, which he frames as needing a different 'mix of skills' as AI changes what work means.
highlights: Decoder interviews Atlassian CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes on the SaaSpocalypse and enterprise AI
Bear case: agents read across tools, or AI builds the tools outright and kills the category
Cannon-Brookes: design and human users matter, and AI is increasing Atlassian usage
All Atlassian products are framed as expressions of one core platform
This year's layoffs were about a different 'mix of skills', per the CEO
He argues chatbots are not the future of work
